item.title: Scientists fitted GPS collars to 17 lions and 14 hyenas expecting hyenas to follow lions
item.description: A groundbreaking study suggests that it's the male lions that approach spotted hyenas, contrary to the belief that hyenas seek out lion remains for food. In fact, spotted hyenas are known to back away from lions, prioritizing their safety. This finding highlights the importance of spatial avoidance in hyena behavior, emphasizing their adaptive strategies to circumvent confrontations with such powerful hunters.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Instead of managing billions, Warren Buffett’s son Howard Buffett chose farming
item.description: Choosing a path less traveled, Howard Buffett, the son of Warren Buffett, dedicated his life to farming and conservation rather than finance. He skillfully managed farms in Nebraska and Illinois, prioritizing soil health. Warren Buffett supported his passion by purchasing a Nebraska farm for his son. As he transitions to the role of non-executive chairman at Berkshire Hathaway, Howard aims to safeguard the company’s culture following his father's legacy.

item.title: After husband’s death, she ensured their 215 acres stay protected
item.description: Becky Shelton made a conscious decision to prioritize land preservation over lucrative offers from developers. By securing her properties in King George and Stafford with legal protections, she ensures these areas remain untouched for future custodians. Shelton views her role as a temporary steward of the earth, taking action to prevent the encroachment of subdivisions and data centers on the natural landscape.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US court rules 150,000 Mississippi residents have no constitutional right to lead-free water
item.description: A federal appeals court has determined that the US Constitution does not explicitly provide a right to clean drinking water. Residents of Jackson residents claimed their city was aware of unsafe water conditions but chose to mislead them. Although the court acknowledged the severity of these claims, it denied the establishment of a constitutional right to safe water and pointed to different legal recourses.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A San Francisco house worth $4.4 million changed hands through disputed deeds in little over a year
item.description: In a dramatic legal move, San Francisco authorities have initiated a lawsuit to annul eight contentious deeds associated with a luxurious $4.4 million property in the prestigious Sea Cliff area. This case has been characterized by officials as a complex scheme aimed at seizing control of the estate. After over a year of dubious ownership transitions, the city aims to rectify property records and reaffirm the rightful ownership.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2002, San Antonio gave an Air Force base for redevelopment; 24 years later, it is expanding
item.description: San Antonio’s Brooks Development Authority is expanding beyond the former 1,308-acre Air Force base it has redeveloped since 2002. It will take control of 243 vacant acres along Southton Road and prepare the site with roads and utilities. The move aims to attract major employers and extend development across the city’s Southeast Side.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: From 2017-19, Japan recycled 6.21M phones into 5,000 Tokyo Olympic and Paralympic medals
item.description: Japan embarked on a groundbreaking initiative ahead of the 2020 Olympic and Paralympic Games, gathering millions of used electronics and phones. This effort resulted in the extraction of significant gold, silver, and bronze from these devices by recyclers. The recovered metals were then transformed into the medals awarded at the events, reflecting a nationwide commitment to sustainability and innovative recycling practices involving local municipalities and businesses.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Montana seals 20 hazards at five abandoned uranium sites that once supplied US defence program
item.description: Several abandoned uranium mine sites in Montana’s Pryor Mountains have been closed after assessments found physical hazards, radiation and chemical contamination risks. The project addressed 20 mine features across five historic sites, while also protecting bat habitat, rare plants and cultural resources. Officials said continued monitoring will be needed because erosion, gravity and vandalism can affect mine closures over time.

item.title: Uber exits Nigeria, Uganda: Why Africa's ride-hailing market is getting tougher
item.description: Uber has officially ended its operations in Nigeria and Uganda, marking a significant retreat from these markets. This decision comes as a result of escalating operating expenses and fierce competition, which have negatively impacted ride-hailing fares and driver earnings. Rising costs for fuel and vehicle upkeep weighed heavily on drivers' incomes. Despite this setback, Uber continues to prioritize other sub-Saharan African markets where growth seems promising.
item.dc:creator: Shivanghi Payal

item.title: In the 1950s, Hugo Meyer bought abandoned Vermont farms; his family has protected 18,000+ acres
item.description: In a remarkable effort, the Meyer family has preserved thousands of acres in the Worcester Range of Vermont, committing to a sustainable approach to timber management. This conservation initiative plays a vital role in protecting significant wildlife corridors and northern hardwood ecosystems, with part of the funding sourced from the U.S. Forest Service's Forest Legacy Program, paving the way for future generations to enjoy the area's natural beauty.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: After losing 75% of wetlands, Niagara River uses recycled Christmas trees to restore fish habitat
item.description: In an innovative approach, conservation teams are utilizing recycled Christmas trees to rejuvenate the coastal wetlands of Niagara River. This dynamic initiative, launched in 2016, spans over 1.64 kilometers, serving to calm wave action and lower erosion rates. By restoring vital aquatic habitats, the project aims to enhance the ecosystem, leading to a remarkable increase in both fish and shorebird populations alongside improved water quality.

item.title: Scientist finds 10,000-year-old mastodon molar while surveying California creek for threatened frogs
item.description: While investigating a creek for frogs, a scientist stumbled upon a remarkable ancient mastodon tooth, estimated to be over ten thousand years old. Paleontologists have confirmed its belonging to a long-extinct species of Pacific mastodon. The fossil will soon be analyzed at Stanford University to determine its precise age, establishing a fascinating connection between today's conservation initiatives and the ancient ecosystems of California.
